IT Portfolio & Capacity Manager

Turn competing IT demands into priorities teams can deliver. In this hands-on role with Group IT Strategy at Systematic, you will connect delivery realities with leadership decisions. Working closely with teams and leadership, you will help shape our evolving portfolio and capacity capability, clarifying what we can commit to, what comes next and what must wait.

The job

Group IT (GRIT) supports Systematic’s business units with infrastructure, systems, integrations, applications and governance. Our Plan-Build-Run model combines sprint-based development, stage-gate projects and Kanban operations to manage and improve services. As IT Portfolio & Capacity Manager, you will connect these delivery models into a trusted view of delivery, commitments and available capacity.

This is a hands-on role, reporting is a part of it, but not all of it. You will work with project managers, delivery teams, architects and leadership, and turn portfolio realities into clear priorities, capacity views, dependencies, risks and delivery expectations. You will move between portfolio decisions with the CIO and GRIT leadership and detailed reviews of project plans or Jira data with delivery teams, challenging commitments, dependencies and capacity assumptions. Your insight will help leadership decide what to prioritise, take on next or defer.

In addition to that, some of your key tasks will be to:

• Create a decision-ready portfolio view across stage-gate projects, sprints and Kanban, keeping commitments, dependencies and decisions visible across Plan-Build-Run.

• Connect demand, commitments and capacity to test delivery feasibility, assessing new demands with the Enterprise Architect and Director of Group IT Strategy.

• Investigate Jira and other delivery data, resolving gaps and inconsistencies with colleagues to establish a trusted portfolio picture.

• Validate progress, plans, dependencies and capacity assumptions directly with project managers and delivery teams, challenging commitments beyond status reports.

• Prepare and facilitate leadership discussions on portfolio priorities, making the impact on existing work, dependencies and capacity clear and following through on decisions and actions.

• Improve portfolio processes and tooling, using automation and AI to reduce manual administration and strengthen transparency and decision support.

Joining the team

The portfolio and capacity management model you will work with is still evolving, and you will play an important role in shaping it. Our ambition is not to build a large administrative PMO. We want a lightweight and trusted portfolio capability that gives us transparency across demand and delivery, helps us make realistic commitments, and enables us to adjust priorities as our capacity and business needs change.

You will become part of the GRIT Strategy team, a small team working across strategy, Enterprise Architecture, portfolio and project management to keep Group IT focused on the right priorities and strengthen the connection between planning and execution. Reporting to the Director of Group IT Strategy, you will take over a running portfolio process from an interim consultant and work closely with project managers, Enterprise Architecture and GRIT leadership.

The team is based in Aarhus. If you are located in Copenhagen, we are open to discussing a hybrid arrangement, but you should expect regular presence in Aarhus, approximately 6–8 days per month.

Your qualifications - most importantly, you understand how work actually gets delivered in an IT organisation.

You have worked close enough to technology delivery to understand the interaction between demand, projects, agile teams, dependencies, capacity and operational commitments. You understand that different teams may plan and deliver work differently, and you are able to create transparency across that complexity without trying to force everything into one delivery model. Your background could be in IT portfolio management, technology delivery, programme management, IT transformation or a PMO role closely integrated with IT delivery. The exact title matters less than your ability to understand delivery and turn fragmented information into a portfolio that can be actively managed. We expect you to have experience with several of the following:

• Experience from portfolio management, IT delivery, programme management, technology transformation or a similar role within an IT organisation.

• A practical understanding of project-based delivery, Scrum/sprint-based delivery and Kanban, and the ability to navigate between these ways of working.

• Experience creating portfolio or capacity views across multiple teams, projects or delivery models.

• The analytical ability to connect demand, capacity, dependencies, commitments and delivery.

• The willingness and ability to work hands-on with the underlying data rather than relying on a separate PMO or reporting organisation to produce it for you.

• Practical experience with Jira or similar delivery management tools.

• Strong analytical capabilities using Excel, Power BI or comparable tools to investigate data and create useful management views.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to turn complex delivery information into clear choices and trade-offs for senior stakeholders.

• Curiosity about how AI and automation can reduce manual portfolio administration and improve decision support.

• Fluent English. Danish is an advantage.

You are structured, curious and persistent

When the portfolio picture is unclear, you do not simply wait for someone to produce another status report. You look into the underlying information, talk to the people involved, challenge assumptions and work out what is actually happening. You enjoy creating order from complexity and are comfortable moving between strategic discussions and delivery detail. You also have the confidence to challenge when things do not add up. If commitments exceed available capacity, dependencies have been overlooked or different sources tell different stories, you make that visible and help the organisation resolve it.

At the same time, you are pragmatic. You understand that perfect data rarely exists in a fast-moving IT organisation and know how to create sufficient transparency to enable decisions without turning portfolio management into bureaucracy. You thrive as a senior specialist who takes ownership of your domain and leads through sound judgement, structure, collaboration and follow-through.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

You should enjoy turning ideas into reality quickly, working with code, data and complex market dynamics to improve the tools that Nitor relies on every day.

Start Date: As soon as possible

Magnus Jónhardsson

mjo@nitorenergy.com

As a Quantitative Analyst at Nitor Energy, you will help advance the models, algorithms and analytical frameworks that power our trading strategies. You will work directly with complex datasets, market dynamics and production-grade code to enhance the accuracy, speed and robustness of our decision-making tools. This role offers hands-on exposure to the full lifecycle of quantitative development in a modern energy-trading company, shaping ideas, testing assumptions and turning data-driven insights into real trading impact.

The Quantitative Analyst we’re looking for is motivated, analytical and want to help elevate our data, models and workflows while accelerating their own development. You should see yourself thriving in a team that executes quickly, turning ideas into production-ready solutions with a pragmatical mindset and sense of ownership.

Your tasks will include

• Work closely with traders to develop and refine quantitative models that support profitable trading strategies

• Continuously seek improvements to workflows, analytics, risk tools, and business processes

• Conduct ad hoc quick analysis to support trading, risk, and commercial decision-making

• Design, develop, and maintain analytic and operational views used for monitoring strategies and market dynamics for trading

• Support the development and maintenance of Python-based models

• Contribute directly to advancing and scaling our data infrastructure

• Hold a Master within a quantitative field

• You have strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills

• Have great python knowledge and an eagerness to code. Other code languages is a plus

• You must be a strong team player

• We expect you to have a pragmatic mindset and get things done

• You have a winning mentality and are willing to go the extra mile to challenge the status quo

• You have a do what it takes mentality and do not take no for an answer

What we offer

• A young, dynamic, ambitious and fun work environment

• Extensive opportunities for personal development and career growth. You will be given responsibility from day one and receive close sparring with experienced colleagues

• The opportunity to contribute and make your mark on the team’s development

• A fun and social work environment with events such as Friday bars, poker tournaments, summer and Christmas parties etc. throughout the year. We also offer weekly sports activities to boost team spirit, such as our Nitor-running club!

• Delicious lunch arrangement with food from Meyers in our own canteen

Our unique culture integrates traders, coders, and analysts into cohesive teams, creating a well-rounded approach to our success. We believe in a balanced work-life dynamic and foster a vibrant, engaging atmosphere where our employees can excel in every aspect.

Developing great products for sports applications in a highly technical and dynamic environment?

Join us on our journey to enable athletes around the world with actionable, data-driven insights. Trackman is expanding with an additional Project Lead to lead the development of our next-generation modular hardware platform designed to serve multiple sports applications, from idea generation through production and into the field. Being a Hardware Project Lead at Trackman requires you to work closely together with several senior stakeholders in a very dynamic environment – driven by our passion for the product, the customer and sports.

The position is in the R&D Hardware department, working closely with all hardware teams – mechanics, optics, electronics, and certification – as well as our close colleagues in embedded software, tracking algorithm teams, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, and production.

The workplace for this position is at our HQ in Science Park DTU in Hørsholm.

Your key responsibilities are

• 
Lead the hardware project group together with the Product Owner(s), developing next-generation hardware for golf and other sports applications.

• 
Translate customer and business needs into clear technical requirements and hardware architecture.

• 
Collaborate with stakeholders across Management, Business Development, Tracking, and Manufacturing to align priorities and ensure progress.

• 
Turn technical requirements into actionable tasks, manage resources and dependencies, and maintain the overall hardware project plan.

• 
Represent Trackman in technical discussions with suppliers, including specifications, quality issues, and expectations.

• 
Communicate project status, progress, risks, and key obstacles clearly to management and other stakeholders.

• 
Coordinate international product certifications, including CE, FCC, and UL, together with the Certification team.

• 
Identify and manage hardware risks related to areas such as product quality, obsolescence, suppliers, and certifications.

Are you our new colleague?

We’re looking for an experienced project manager with a strong hardware engineering background who can bridge technical complexity, business needs, and collaboration. Ideally, you bring:

• 
Several years of project management experience in hardware product development, preferably with RF systems.

• 
Experience with complex projects across mechanics, electronics, RF, and embedded software.

• 
Strong understanding of requirements management, design verification, and product industrialization.

• 
Solid business acumen and the ability to translate diverse user needs into robust product solutions.

• 
Experience with project management methodologies and Agile principles, ideally bringing complex electronics products to market.

• 
Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach, knowing when to listen, challenge, and take the lead.

Who is Trackman

Trackman is a privately-owned company founded in 2003. The company has experienced consistent high growth driven by a market-leading sports ball tracking technology based on radar and vision tracking, sustained by a strong desire to innovate.

The company employs globally more than 1000+ employees and has offices in Denmark (headquarter in Hørsholm), Aarhus, US (Connecticut and Arizona), Japan, South Korea, and Poland.

While being active in multiple sports including baseball, football, and soccer, Trackman is first and foremost a golf company. Trackman has revolutionised the way golf players train and instructors teach, and is now broadening the technology so all golfers can take advantage – whether they are playing indoors, on driving ranges, or on the golf course.

In baseball, Trackman is the leading technology company in the world with solutions for practice, games, and the largest data sharing network, monetised by selling draft data on amateur players to the Major League Baseball teams. Trackman has also developed practice solutions for American Football and Soccer that are now used among top teams.

Trackman has the largest R&D capacity in the industry and is constantly aiming to push the boundaries for sports, technology, and data. We strive to recruit the best talent from around the world for R&D functions such as Hardware. At our HQ in Denmark, we have an R&D team of more than 250 FTEs representing more than 40 countries around the world. Trackman designs, develops, and produces all of our technology from start to finish in-house under one roof.

Trackman’s 12,500 m² state-of-the-art CO₂-neutral headquarter is located in Science Park DTU in Hørsholm.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

Join Saxo’s Enterprise Identity & Data Security (EIDS) team and play a pivotal role in protecting the bank’s most valuable asset it’s data.

About the role

In this role, you will design and implement advanced data protection controls across modern security platforms, with a strong focus on Microsoft Purview and insider risk solutions. You will translate complex regulatory and data risk requirements into scalable, effective technical controls that safeguard sensitive information and strengthen Saxo’s security posture.

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to Saxo’s broader agenda around security, governance, and operational resilience within a highly regulated financial environment, working closely with stakeholders across technology, compliance, and the business.

Your responsibilities

As a Senior Data Security Engineer, you will:

• Design and implement data protection controls across Microsoft Purview (DLP, Information Protection, Insider Risk Management)

• Translate data security risks and regulatory requirements into robust, enforceable technical solutions

• Lead and support the rollout and optimisation of Insider Risk Management and user activity monitoring tools (e.g. Teramind)

• Drive data discovery, classification, and visibility across structured and unstructured data environments

• Monitor, tune, and continuously improve the effectiveness of data protection policies and controls

• Collaborate with security, compliance, and business stakeholders to mitigate data risks and strengthen governance frameworks

Your profile

We are looking for a proactive and technically strong professional who can balance risk, regulation, and real-world implementation:

• 7–10 years of experience in data security or information security engineering

• Hands-on expertise with Microsoft Purview (DLP, labelling, Insider Risk)

• Strong understanding of data protection risks, insider threats, and mitigation strategies

• Experience working in regulated environments (financial services is an advantage)

• Solid knowledge of Microsoft 365, Azure, and enterprise security tooling

• Experience with automation or scripting (e.g. PowerShell, APIs) is a plus

• Relevant certifications such as SC-400 are preferred

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

Would you like the opportunity to get some hands-on experience in finance business partnering and lay the foundation for a career in Finance? Do you want to create real impact by identifying key cost and value drivers? Do you want to become a part of an international company that contributes to the green transition?

Here is what the job entails

As our student worker in Controlling, you will play a key role in supporting our Finance Business Partnering team by handling data, conducting analysis, and collaborating with stakeholders to solve business challenges. You will be ensuring timely and high-quality execution of tasks, while contributing to process improvements through data modelling. Furthermore, you will be assisting with various tasks such as creating instructions as well as supporting team members during peak loads.

More specifically, you will be:

• Ensuring accuracy and quality in resource allocation data

• Keeping Project data up to date, including control of capitalization on projects

• Supporting the maintenance and reporting on our Standard Cost

• Assisting the team with various analysis, modelling and controlling activities

In this role, you will gain hands-on experience with financial controlling and data-driven decision-making in an international company. You will develop strong analytical and stakeholder management skills while working closely with experienced colleagues on real business challenges.

Meet your future team

You will join our Finance Business Partnering team of 9 colleagues, who act as the primary Finance stakeholders for each Division and Functional Area across Kamstrup. Our focus is to ensure the highest quality of business reporting, which in turn allows us to use the data for problem solving to create real value for the company. Our team is offered a lot of responsibility, which in turn means that we set the bar high for ourselves and the results that we produce. Despite this, we have an informal atmosphere in the team, where inputs and perspectives from all team members are highly valued.

Did you know? Our team is quite diverse in terms of personality types, making collaboration in the team, and the solutions we produce, much more dynamic.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for an enthusiastic and ambitious student who is eager to apply their knowledge of finance and business controlling while making a real impact on our team. You take pride in your work and have a great overview and structured approach, ensuring that your deadlines are met with a high degree of quality.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are studying a degree in Economics, Business Administration, or another relevant field

• Are curious and enjoy proactively seeking new challenges where you can gain knowledge and new perspectives

• Have a structured approach to your work and thrive in managing your tasks efficiently and effectively

• Enjoy collaboration and have good communication skills, enabling you to interact and build relationships within and outside of Kamstrup

• Are well acquainted with Excel and other MS office tools

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

We are more than an ordinary workplace

We offer a challenging student job in an international company where you are given independent responsibility for specific assignments, and where you can transform your theoretical knowledge into practical experience. As a student worker, you will be treated as an integrated part of the team, equal to other employees, ensuring a steep learning curve.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work-life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Are you a design or verification engineer with ASIC/FPGA skills, and do you have a flair for client communication? If so, then SyoSil has a great career opportunity for you.

SyoSil will soon initiate a new project, for which we search for new team members to join our existing staff of 20 highly qualified ASIC engineers. We both look for seniors as well as newly graduated engineers.

The project will focus on digital design and verification for an RF radio ASIC, being part of a large international multi-team project. In this project, SyoSil will assume the full responsibility of several IP blocks, from architecture definition towards RTL design and coverage driven verification closure. Design and verification will be done using SystemVerilog and UVM. The project management will be SCRUM based.

We offer:

• A challenging role where you work closely with a highly skilled team as well as interfacing to engineers in leading international companies

• Access to the latest technologies and ongoing professional development, including training with ASIC tools from the top EDA vendors in the SyoSil partnership portfolio

• A competitive salary and a flexible working environment

**Join an international team of specialists

**

You will join a young and dynamic team of 20 engineers in a vibrant international environment close to central Copenhagen, Denmark. **

Interested?

Are you passionate about finding new drug opportunities? Do you love understanding disease biology to guide the best possible drug design? Are you a seasoned professional and looking for the next step?

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives. Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to demonstrate strong stakeholder management and communication skills, high personal and scientific integrity and the ability to navigate complex environments.

Travel: 20-30days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

jobs.occupation: Senior Process Automation Engineer in DCS at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Senior Process Automation Engineer in DCS, Novo Nordisk Engineering

Do you want to be a part of NNE’s all-time largest Process Automation team? We are looking for colleagues to join our fantastic company, where we have the aspiration of becoming best in class within Automation Solutions for Pharmaceutical Engineering.

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

You will be working in an enthusiastic Process Automation team with more than 80 colleagues in Denmark. Globally, the Process Automation team has more than 200 employees.

The Process Automation team works with consultancy, design & development, implementation and validation of Automation solutions for the Pharma and Biotech industries. Our work is project based, and currently we are looking into an exciting pipeline of large data driven, greenfield plants with modular/scalable designs.

We are skilled in a broad range of process areas within API production e.g. fermentation, recovery and purification, utility, and cleaning systems. And the solutions we provide to our customers are always based on a deep understanding of the customers’ production processes – and if standard components can’t do the job, we develop our own.

How you might spend your days

As a DCS Senior Process Automation Engineer, you’ll be:

• Advising customers on their application process solutions

• Design developing, programming, commissioning, qualifying, FAT, SAT, UAT and Handover of applications for Distributed Control Systems (DCS)

• Interacting with process experts and colleagues with expertise in surrounding systems and equipment like MES, Historian systems, instruments, production equipment etc.

• Developing and optimizing automation methods and strategies to meet our customers’ needs and sharing working knowledge with colleagues and partners

• Forming the basis of automation strategies and architectures to support our sister departments internationally and expand NNE’s Process Automation engagement

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Understand your colleagues’ individual and cultural difference

• Are aware of your surroundings and able to flag any concerns

• Are agile and able to prioritize urgent tasks

• Are team-oriented and able to collaborate on team projects

• Are reliable, curious and eager to learn

• Are appreciative of feedback, because it contributes to your growth

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• You have 6+ years or more of working experience and hold a degree as an engineer, ideally within electrical, automation, process or marine engineering

• You have 4 years or more of working experience with PCS/DCS Application development (for example ABB 800xA or ABB SattLine), working in GMP/GAMP environment or with execution of Automation projects

• Knowledge of batch production is valued

• You find the complexity of the GMP/GAMP environment exciting

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 13th December 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Christian Ljørring on +45 30 79 29 08 or Manager Rasmus Sølbeck Hansen +45 31 91 89 30

Please note:

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

The candidate

What we offer

Working with Welltec® means challenges and personal development in a demanding work environment. It is exciting and rewarding, and it is a varied place to work. jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026 – Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU), Copenhagen, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Position:

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is seeking candidates for its newly established Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026. These internship opportunities are on-site at SCMU’s office in the UN City headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark.

SCMU offers specialized functional streams aligned with its operational needs, including:

• Data & Analytics

• Logistics & Supply Chain

• Procurement & Business

• Humanitarian Supplies

• Supply Chain & Customer Service

• Governance, Risk & Compliance

• Communications

• Human Resources

• Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

• Administration & Business

To ensure effective team integration and maximize the value of the internship, candidates must be logistically and financially prepared to undertake full-time, on-site work in Copenhagen for the duration of the internship.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.  UNFPA’s strategic plan (2026-2029), reaffirms the relevance of the current strategic direction of UNFPA and focuses on three transformative results: to end preventable maternal deaths; end unmet need for family planning; and end gender-based violence and harmful practices. These results capture our strategic commitments on accelerating progress towards realizing the ICPD and SDGs in the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. Our strategic plan calls upon UN Member States, organizations and individuals to “build forward better”, while addressing the negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on women’s and girls’ access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, recover lost gains and realize our goals.

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is self-funded and was made operational in January 2022. It is tasked with ensuring that UNFPA is able to effectively and efficiently support the delivery of life-saving reproductive health products and other programme supplies to the end user when and where they are needed. To achieve this, it is important to strengthen the capacity of governments and implementing partners to ensure coordination, end-to-end visibility and accountability on all supply chain and logistics management related activities, in particular for programme supplies, across all UNFPA programmes.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results.

Eligibility:

Educational requirements

a. Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year;

b. Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher);

c. Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or

d. Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Other eligibility requirements

e. Demonstrate interest in the field of development;

f.  Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and

g. Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds.

An individual whose father, mother, son, daughter, brother or sister is a UNFPA staff member is not eligible for an internship with UNFPA.

Required Competencies:

Values:

• Exemplifying integrity,

• Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,

• Embracing cultural diversity,

• Embracing change

Core Competencies:

• Achieving results,

• Being accountable,

• Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,

• Thinking analytically and strategically,

• Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,

Financial Support:

Interns who do not receive financial support from an outside party (such as an academic institution, university, government) are eligible to receive a stipend as a contribution towards living expenses. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. The stipend is normally paid in local currency at the end of each month.
